assumptions_and_caveats: No web access: all pricing and feature claims reflect Claude training knowledge (cutoff Jan 2026) and published EUR list prices on annual billing; verify against current vendor quotes before signing. Assumes 40 paid sales/account-management seats, EU (Dublin) entity, no existing CRM data migration constraints.
salesforce_capabilities: Salesforce Sales Cloud is the depth leader: fully customisable objects, advanced workflow/Flow automation, strong reporting, Einstein AI scoring, and the largest third-party marketplace (AppExchange). Real ad-agency fit usually also requires Marketing Cloud or Pardot/Account Engagement, sold separately, plus admin or partner resources to configure and maintain.
salesforce_pricing_eur: Sales Cloud list (EUR/user/month, annual): Starter ~25, Pro Suite ~80, Enterprise ~165, Unlimited ~330. Realistic tier for a 40-seat agency is Enterprise: ~40 x 165 = ~6,600/month, ~79,200/year, before Marketing Cloud add-ons, sandboxes, premier support, or implementation partner fees (commonly 20-50k one-off).
salesforce_strengths_weaknesses: Strengths: unmatched configurability, enterprise reporting, ecosystem, scales far beyond 40 seats. Weaknesses: highest TCO by 2-4x, needs a dedicated admin (~0.5-1 FTE), slow time-to-value (3-6 month implementations typical), UI complexity drives adoption risk in creative-agency cultures.
hubspot_capabilities: HubSpot is a unified CRM + marketing platform: Sales Hub (pipeline, sequences, forecasting), native Ads tool that manages and attributes Meta Ads, Google Ads and LinkedIn campaigns inside the CRM, built-in email/landing pages, and strong out-of-the-box reporting. Setup is largely self-serve; admin burden is low.
hubspot_pricing_eur: Post-2024 seat pricing (EUR/user/month, annual, approx): Sales Hub Pro ~90, Enterprise ~150; core seats can be mixed with cheaper view-only seats. Modelled 25 Sales Pro seats + 15 lighter seats plus Marketing Hub Pro (~800/month flat, contact-tiered): roughly 3,300-4,200/month, ~40-50k/year all-in. Marketing Hub costs rise with contact database size - a real variable for an agency running campaigns.
hubspot_strengths_weaknesses: Strengths: best native ad-ops alignment (Meta/Google Ads sync, ad ROI attribution to deals), fastest adoption curve, marketing and sales in one data model, EU data hosting (Frankfurt). Weaknesses: per-seat cost climbs steeply at Enterprise tier, custom-object and permission flexibility below Salesforce, contact-based marketing pricing can surprise.
zoho_capabilities: Zoho CRM covers core SFA well (pipelines, workflows, Zia AI assist, Canvas UI customisation) and sits inside the broader Zoho One suite (campaigns, desk, books). Functionally credible for mid-market, with EU data centres (Amsterdam/Dublin).
zoho_pricing_eur: EUR/user/month, annual: Standard ~14, Professional ~23, Enterprise ~40, Ultimate ~52. 40 seats on Enterprise: ~1,600/month, ~19,200/year - roughly 40% of HubSpot and 25% of Salesforce cost. Zoho One bundle (~37-45/user/month) adds the full suite for marginal extra cost.
zoho_strengths_weaknesses: Strengths: decisive price leader, generous feature-per-euro, low lock-in. Weaknesses: weakest native ad-platform integrations (Google Ads connector exists; Meta lead sync is shallow and often needs Zapier/Make), patchier UX consistency, smaller partner ecosystem in Ireland, brand perception may hamper exec buy-in.
ad_ops_integration_fit: Meta/Google Ads: HubSpot native and bidirectional (audiences, lead sync, cost + attribution); Salesforce strong but via paid add-ons (Marketing Cloud, AppExchange connectors like LeadsBridge); Zoho partial, connector-dependent. GA4: all three integrate via connectors; HubSpot and Salesforce have mature first/third-party options, Zoho relies more on middleware. Programmatic (DV360, The Trade Desk, Amazon DSP): no CRM has true native support - plan on Supermetrics/Funnel for cost data ingestion and a reverse-ETL or LiveRamp-style path for audience activation regardless of vendor; HubSpot and Salesforce have the broader certified-partner coverage here.
comparative_summary: For a 40-person Dublin ad agency: Salesforce is over-scoped and over-priced unless enterprise-client procurement demands it; Zoho is the budget hedge but fights the agency's ad-ops workflow; HubSpot lands the best capability-to-adoption-to-cost balance, with native Meta/Google Ads attribution that directly matches agency reporting needs at ~40-50k EUR/year.
